- **House precedent for bounding a self-service shield.** The #1961 per-pod
  named shield is ceiling-bounded (`EPM_POD_NAMED_SHIELD_MAX_AGE_H`, 48h); the
  #1582 keep-running wedged-owner arm escalates a tagged pod with a provably
  wedged owner. Both are the pattern for "honour the signal, bound the
  window".

## Decision: bounded DEFER + ESCALATE, not unbounded suppress

Wire it, but as a **time-bounded deferral with escalation**, not a
`keep-running`-style unconditional skip.

- **Why not plain suppress.** Unlike the `keep-running` tag, a fence is a token
  any session can self-post with no operator action. An unconditional
  fence-skip creates an unbounded self-service pod-alive shape with no
  wedged-owner arm behind it — the fence-refresh-forever risk row in #2277
  plan §8, on the one pass whose entire purpose is reclaiming spend from
  provably parked/terminal tasks.
- **Why not surface-only.** Surfacing without deferring leaves the stop to
  land, so it does not close the stated Goal harm (an in-flight owner round
  interrupted) at all.
- **Shape.** When the status-class arm would `stop` a pod that carries an
  UNEXPIRED fence AND whose latest pod-bound PASS lacks the matching `owner=`
  (the terminate guard's exact predicate — owner presumed live), DEFER the
  stop and escalate once per episode (marker + push + sidecar) naming the pod,
  the fence expiry, and the hourly burn. Two bounds: the fence's own
  `fence_until` (primary — expiry re-arms the ordinary auto-stop by
  construction) and a cumulative per-(issue, pod_id) deferral ceiling that
  closes refresh-forever, with a loud escalation at the ceiling.
- **Directionally safe.** The arm can only ever DEFER a stop, never accelerate
  one, so no watcher path becomes more willing to stop a pod than it is today
  (the standing pod directive). Fail-open on every unreadable input (#2277's
  posture); kill switch for rollback; the ≥2-miss accumulation,
  `keep-running` shield, follow-up-signal predicate, and #1961 per-pod named
  shield all preserved unchanged.

Non-goals unchanged: `pod.py terminate` is not re-opened, and the declared
copied-token residual (unauthenticated string equality) stays open under the
same accidents-not-adversaries trust model.

## The two blockers, both real, both verified against live code before acceptance

**1. Alternatives r1 — a self-posted fence would have countermanded an explicit USER PAUSE.** `POD_SAFETY_AUTO_STOP = AUTO_STOP_DONE | AUTO_STOP_PAUSED` (:1454) and `_status_class` (:13450) collapses both into the single `"auto-stop-done"` string, so v1's arm — keyed on that string — silently inherited the `on_hold` member. On the DONE members the pass reclaims an escaped pod; on `on_hold` it is EXECUTING the user's own pause directive (#980). Deferring there means an agent's self-posted token overrides the user for up to `min(fence_until, 24h)` — the standing pod directive inverted. **Fix in v2:** raw status threaded to the single eligibility site, gated on `status in AUTO_STOP_DONE` (set membership, not a `!= "on_hold"` string test, so future enum growth routes correctly). Nothing legitimate lost — `_task_followup_active` requires a signal NEWER than the latest done-transition, which a pause posts, so a compliant post-pause round is already `followup-skip`-shielded. Pinned by two rows.

**2. Methodology r2 — the ceiling would have gone structurally inert on any multi-pod issue.** v2 specced the episode fields on the singular `kr_owner_*` family, which resets on `kr_same_pod = (prev or {}).get("pod_id") == pod_id` (:14578) against a payload holding ONE `pod_id` slot (:14608) — while `_process_pod` runs AND SAVES per pod. On the routine primary + `--name-suffix` shape every sibling save would reset the fenced pod's fields each tick: the 24h ceiling never exhausts (voiding the bound §4.1 leans on to justify DEFER over an unconditional skip), the once-per-episode marker re-fires every ~10 min, and the evaluated-and-inactive CARRY rule is destroyed. All 23 v2 test rows were single-pod, so the plan would have certified green properties that fail on the demonstrated fleet shape. **This is the same defect the #2149 review Must-Fixed in this very function** — the `kr_pod` sub-dict exists because of it and its docstring (:14598-14603) names that Must-Fix. **Fix in v3:** episode state moved to a pod_id-keyed `fd_pod` sub-dict on the `kr_pod`/`nr_pod` contract (sibling entries forward-carried verbatim, per-pod keying IS the incarnation reset, GC'd against `issue_running_pod_ids`) — which also DELETED the hand-wired-reset duty v2 had imposed on the implementer. Pinned by two multi-pod rows, one interleaving ≥2 RUNNING pods per tick and asserting both entry survival and on-schedule exhaustion.

## Other applied findings

- Tri-state fence-read wrapper (`True`/`False`/`None`) — a bool conflated a transient read failure with a definite "no fence", so a failure would CLEAR the ceiling and widen the refresh-forever hole. DEFER stays fail-open (`fence_active = result is True`); only the episode-clear consults the third state.
- Episode-clear keyed on EVALUATED-and-inactive, not not-observed-active — under lazy evaluation a shield handover would otherwise leave a stale onset that reads instantly-exhausted against a fresh fence.
- Residual gap re-characterized: three shapes, not two (the #1961 named shield already covers suffixed pods for 48h). Error direction was conservative; wiring decision unaffected.
- Rejected fourth option recorded (pod-side liveness-probe conjunct — wrong in both failure directions).
- Named consequences/residuals: wedge fall-through billing to the ceiling; lapse-recycle ceiling reset; CARRY-across-long-handover.
- Two factual self-corrections: the watcher DOES import `datetime` at :1207 (round-1 C5 was wrong and v2 propagated it); the owner-fence test count is not cited as an acceptance number.

The fence-defer arm is therefore strictly MORE bounded than the shield the fleet already accepts — pod-scoped, deadline-carrying, 24h-ceilinged. Recorded in §4.1.
